<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx`  _(via resolveI18nLabel (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`  _(via resolveI18nLabel (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **224** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **161** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **161**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **57** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **180** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `42a7567352d64da3fd17b36a87edb01e8834361c` — the merge of head `6e8b63894022174bb53a869f49d38eb05e85173d` into base `3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 42a7567352d64da3fd17b36a87edb01e8834361c && git checkout 42a7567352d64da3fd17b36a87edb01e8834361c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db 6e8b63894022174bb53a869f49d38eb05e85173d && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db && git merge --no-ff 6e8b63894022174bb53a869f49d38eb05e85173d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3f61e4f8fb567160f839c3269ee95aa89ee4f1db` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4d0fb81ba5cd58ea1e42c02f15d8f033677a7eba`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts + ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/i18nLabel-resolver-parity.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/cli/test/i18n-inline-locale-map-coverage.test.ts

Inputs: card #30910 (body, triage 6683176666, claim 6684338116, amendment 6684414838, progress request 6695504263, os-dev-report 6700059771), PR #31068 (body, 9-file list, net diff against `main` `5210acfbaee`), the check-runs on the head. The rest of the diff (`ui/packages/i18n/**`, the two spec/ui/plugin-list test files, the two changesets) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; the cited files above were READ to judge the `hits` file, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Face.** `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts` is a published spec source ⇒ `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, schema face. Right; matches the claim amendment's "review owed".
- **Public surface of `@objectstack/spec`.** `resolveI18nLabel(label, locale)` keeps its signature and return shape; its BEHAVIOUR changes for one input class (an inline map holding entries of both Chinese scripts, read at a `zh*` locale). `scriptEntryKey` is module-private; `src/ui/index.ts` is untouched. New intra-package runtime import `ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts → system/platform-locales.ts` (no cycle: `platform-locales.ts` imports nothing). Right.
- **No schema change.** `InlineLocaleMapSchema` / `I18nLabelSchema` untouched; what an author can write is unchanged ⇒ `Metadata-protocol: none`. Right.
- **`@object-ui/i18n` gains a runtime dependency edge** on `@objectstack/spec/system` (`PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS`, `platformLocaleTagOf`). `ui/packages/i18n/package.json` already declares `@objectstack/spec: workspace:^` on the head (from #30902, merged in); spec is `sideEffects: false` so the `system` barrel tree-shakes. Neither `package.json` nor `pnpm-lock.yaml` is touched, as the amendment forbade. Right.
- **Table-derived split, no local list.** Both twins read "is this language split by script" off `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS` (count of tags sharing the base, `zh` ⇒ 2) and "which script does a key mean" off `platformLocaleTagOf` (closed alias list, case-folded). Traced the two implementations side by side (spec `scriptEntryKey` vs ui `localizedEntryKey`): limb order exact → own-script base → own-script sibling → base → first sibling is identical, both include the bare base key in the sibling scan, both treat non-string/inherited entries as misses. `pt`, `en`, `es`, `ja`, `fr` fall out of the split check (one table tag each) ⇒ byte-identical to `main`. Right.
- **Two existing vectors flipped** (`{ 'zh-TW', 'zh-CN' }` at `zh` now Simplified, in `pickLocalized.test.ts` and the spec parity table). Right: bare `zh` means `zh-Hans` per `PLATFORM_LOCALE_READ_ALIASES`; the "first sibling in authoring order" rule is re-pinned on `pt-PT`/`pt-BR` and `es-MX`/`es-ES`, where the table names the language once.
- **Reference-copy pin.** The spec test's verbatim copy now cites blob `37b88c07aeb`, which equals the head blob of `ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts` (diff index `a72b5e48363..37b88c07aeb`); the copied helpers are byte-equal to the source save the `Reference` suffix. Right. (No gate enforces this pin; it is prose only, as on `main`.)
- **Docs drift bot** named `content/docs/protocol/kernel/i18n-standard.mdx` and `content/docs/ui/translations.mdx`; read both: neither states the sibling-order limb, so no doc edit is owed by this diff. Right.
- **Check-runs on the head** at review time: every completed run is `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build UI Deps, Auto Label, Check PR Size, Flag docs, among them). STILL IN PROGRESS: Test UI (1/16–16/16), Test Core (1/8–8/8), Build Core, Build & E2E UI, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Type Check · workspace. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts and are not pre-empted here; the ④ finding below does not depend on them (no existing test covers the shape).

### ② Semver level

- Two changesets: `@objectstack/spec` **patch**, `@object-ui/i18n` **patch**. Both carry `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, as does the PR body; Check Changeset is green.
- Patch is right: a behaviour fix to an existing function under the ruled parity contract (#6761 B), no signature, type or schema change, no export added or removed. A consumer that relied on authoring order for a two-script map sees a different entry; that is the defect being fixed, not a surface change.
- `Clause-②:` line: `no` — correct; the diff narrows nothing and declares no new capability.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (os-dev-report 6700059771 and PR body), each answered:

1. **"Live check owed … NOT MEASURED"** (a `zh-Hant` console, nav item + list label over `{ en, zh-CN, zh-TW }`). Acknowledged; not measurable from this read-only seat either. Stays owed to the seat before ACCEPT. Not escalated.
2. **Case asymmetry** (base comparison case-sensitive, new script limb folds via `platformLocaleTagOf`; carrier: contract reviewer). Weighed: pre-existing on `main`, documented and pinned in both twins; the new limb only reorders keys the case-sensitive base comparison already admitted (`ZH-HANT` still falls to `en`, pinned), so it adds no new inconsistency class. Not a defect of this PR; not escalated. Triage may file it as a product question if a `ZH-*` locale is ever observed in a session.
3. **Deviation: surface widened** to the spec twin and the plugin-list parity test — covered by claim amendment 6684414838; the diff's file list matches the amended surface exactly and touches none of the ⛔ files. Right.
4. **Deviation: two vectors flipped** — judged right in ①.
5. **`open_questions: []`**, **`security_findings: none`** — nothing to escalate; the resolver reads own string properties only, and the new limb reads a frozen `Map` (`TAG_BY_FOLDED_CODE`), so a prototype-named locale still misses.
6. **Claim 6700070395 / withdrawal 6700080275**: the dev session withdrew its own review claim; the seat's claim 6700108794 governs this head. Right.

Unflagged by the dev, raised here: the PR body's "the spec twin, which the nav, app shell, components and service-analytics call, keeps agreeing with `pickLocalized`" covers the READ side only; the nav designer's WRITE side was not examined — see ④ M1.

### ④ Design judgment

`hits`: `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts`, judged against the ruling it implements (#6761 B: one shared resolver, limb-for-limb parity with `pickLocalized`), the card's rule 2 ("one reading for both limbs, never two copies") and its first consumers (`ui/packages/app-shell` nav/preview, `plugin-list`, `service-analytics`), with the parity partner, the parity pin and the locale table read in the live tree.

**Holds:** the limb itself. `scriptEntryKey` and `localizedEntryKey` agree on every shape I could construct (both-script maps in any order, bare `zh` with either script, alias spellings `zh-Hans-CN` / `zh-Hant-TW`, unnamed `zh-Hant-US`, one-script maps, non-`zh` languages, `zh-hant` lower-case, `ZH-HANT`); the parity test on the head pins five two-script rows on BOTH functions plus the one-pass "no divergence" sweep; the spec vectors are asserted against the verbatim reference copy first. The first-consumer read sites (`UnifiedSidebar`, `HomePage`, `DraftChangesPanel`, `ListView` aria, `analytics-service`, `dataset-compiler`) call `resolveI18nLabel` and take the fix for free.

**M1 — must-fix. The change splits read from write in the Studio nav designer for a map shape the PR itself names as in reach.**
`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts` — `ownEntryKey` (the key `renamedLabel` writes and `clearedLabel` deletes, used by `AppNavInspector.tsx:292`, `AppNavCanvas.tsx:389`, `SourcePageProperties.tsx:78`) is a third copy of the first limbs: `[tag, tag.split('-')[0]].find(own)`. Its docstring states the invariant it relies on: "The entry written is the one `resolveI18nLabel` reads first for this locale — the exact tag, else its bare language … so the editor shows the new text straight after the edit." This PR makes that false. Trace on the head, locale `zh-Hant` (likewise `zh-TW`, `zh-HK`, `zh-MO`), map `{ en: 'Customer', zh: '客户', 'zh-TW': '客戶' }` — the `bare zh + zh-TW` row of the PR's own `BOTH_SCRIPTS` table:
  - `resolveI18nLabel` → exact miss → `scriptEntryKey`: base `zh` means `zh-Hans` ≠ `zh-Hant`, skipped; sibling `zh-TW` means `zh-Hant` → reads **`zh-TW`** (`客戶`). Correct, and what the designer now displays.
  - `ownEntryKey` → `zh-Hant` absent → **`zh`**. `renamedLabel` overwrites the Simplified `zh` text with the Traditional edit; the field keeps showing the untouched `zh-TW` text (the edit appears to do nothing). `clearedLabel` deletes the Simplified `zh` entry while the Traditional text stays on screen.
  On `main` both read `zh` (limb 2 before limb 3), so the pair agreed; the divergence is introduced by this head. It is the card's harm — a Traditional editor overwriting or deleting Simplified text with a stale Traditional display — moved one consumer over, and it is exactly the "split one console session" the claim amendment widened the surface to prevent. Fix in this PR: route `ownEntryKey` through the shared limb (the simplest seat is `setLocalized` / `clearLocalized` from `@object-ui/i18n`, which app-shell already imports in `DashboardWidgetInspector` and `ReportDefaultInspector`; or export the key picker once and call it from both), and pin `renamedLabel` / `clearedLabel` against `resolveI18nLabel` on the two-script rows in `navItemLabel.inherit-11196.test.ts` (today it has no `zh-TW` / `zh-Hant` vector). The `{ 'zh-CN', 'zh-TW' }` shape is unaffected (neither key is exact or bare, so a `zh-Hant` entry is added and then read exactly); the defect needs a bare `zh` key beside a Traditional one.

**S1 — should-fix. A third limb copy in the coverage gate now disagrees with the twins and its pin is blind to it.**
`packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts` `inlineLocaleText` restates limbs 1–3 (exact, base, first sibling in authoring order) and documents itself as pinned to `resolveI18nLabel`: "whenever this says covered, the renderer really shows that entry". On the head, `{ 'zh-CN': '客户', 'zh-TW': '客戶' }` at `zh-Hant`: coverage says the reader sees `客户`, the renderer shows `客戶`. The covered / not-covered verdict is unchanged (both are hits), so `check:i18n-coverage` still gates correctly; but the pin `packages/cli/test/i18n-inline-locale-map-coverage.test.ts` ("a covered locale is the entry the renderer picks") has no two-script map in its fixture set and stays green by omission, and the docstring names a test file (`inline-locale-coverage-parity.test.ts`) that does not exist in the tree. Add a two-script row to that pin and either take the script limb there too or narrow the docstring's claim to "a covered locale is a locale the renderer answers from the same language" (the coverage question only needs the language, not the script).

**S2 — should-fix (prose in the `hits` file).** The resolver header still says changing the case asymmetry "is a two-repo decision" and names "objectui" as the reference's home; this very PR edits both twins in one commit of one repo, and the test header was already re-pointed to `objectstack-ai/objectstack`. Also the rule table lists the "2–3 …own script first" row after limb 3, while the code runs it before limb 2; the row label says "2–3" but a reader following the table top-down gets the wrong order. One-line fixes.

**S3 — should-fix (file, do not block).** The write side on a ONE-script map still crosses scripts: a `zh-Hant` edit over `{ en, 'zh-CN' }` or `{ en, zh }` writes Traditional text into the Simplified key, and a clear deletes it (pinned as "unchanged" controls in `setLocalized.test.ts`). It honours the WYSIWYG invariant (the editor was showing that entry as a fallback), and the card's stated reach is maps with both keys, so it is out of scope here — but it is the same harm one key short, and the `zh-Hant` console that #30902 adds makes it reachable. Worth a card: should a write in a split-script language whose script has no entry ADD under the session tag instead of replacing the other script's entry?

Observations, no action: the closed alias list means `zh-Hant-US` is not treated as Traditional (pinned both sides; a ruled table property, #29349 F, not this PR's). `PLATFORM_LOCALE_TAGS.filter(...)` runs per call on an 11-row frozen array; negligible.

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2d5cae2c8dc5f85722530c7bc7e0421b37e119d7`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts + ui/packages/i18n/src/pickLocalized.ts, ui/packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/i18nLabel-resolver-parity.test.ts, packages/spec/src/system/platform-locales.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/navItemLabel.inherit-11196.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts, packages/cli/test/i18n-inline-locale-map-coverage.test.ts

Delta review of the FAIL recorded on `4d0fb81ba5` (comment 6700222070). Inputs: card #30910 (body and every comment through the claim amendment 6700234158), PR #31068 (body, 13-file list, net diff against `main` `5210acfbaee`, the delta `4d0fb81ba5..2d5cae2c8d`: commits `7422324200`, `4b4e003685`, `2d5cae2c8d`), the check-runs on the head. Everything judged on `4d0fb81ba5` and unchanged in the delta (the resolver limb, `pickLocalized.ts`, the parity pins, the two changesets) stands as recorded there and is restated only where the delta touches it. The rest of the diff is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; cited files were READ to judge the `hits` file, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Face.** `packages/spec/src/ui/i18n-label-resolver.ts` is still the one `hits` path ⇒ `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, schema face. The delta's change to it is prose only (commit `2d5cae2c8d`): no code, no export, no import moved. Right.
- **Published surface, delta.** `@objectstack/spec`: unchanged from the first record (signature kept, behaviour changed for two-script maps only). `@objectstack/cli` (published, in the `fixed` group): `inlineLocaleText` is an exported function of `src/utils/i18n-coverage.ts`; its signature and its defined/undefined contract are unchanged, its returned TEXT changes only for a two-script map read at a `zh*` locale (see ④). New runtime import `@objectstack/spec/ui` into the cli — `@objectstack/spec` is already a `dependencies` entry (`workspace:*`) and `packages/cli/src/commands/generate.ts` already imports `@objectstack/spec/ui` at runtime, so no new dependency edge and no phantom-import risk. Right.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`** is `private: true`; `navItemLabel.ts` is internal (not exported from the package root) and `resolveI18nLabel` was already imported there on `main`. No public-surface change. Right.
- **Surface vs claim.** The 13-file list equals the amended surface (6684414838 + 6700234158) exactly; `package.json` files and `pnpm-lock.yaml` untouched. Right.
- **Spec test's reference-copy pin** (`37b88c07aeb`) is the blob of `pickLocalized.ts`, which the delta does not touch. Still right.
- **Check-runs on `2d5cae2c8d`** at review time: completed and green — Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check PR Size, Flag docs, Auto Label, filter (the rest skipped by design). STILL IN PROGRESS: Build Core, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Test Core (1/8–8/8), Type Check · workspace / consumer gates / source gates / debt ledger, Lint · ESLint / PM dispatch-gates / repo & tooling gates / docs & code guards / CI, release & engine gates / scoped (query-options erasure, slot lookup & corpus, tooling self-tests). NOT YET STARTED (behind Build UI Deps): Test UI 1/16–16/16, Type Check UI, Lint UI, Build & E2E UI. Their conclusions are the gate verdicts; nothing below pre-empts them. The two new test blocks (`navItemLabel.inherit-11196.test.ts` #30910 describe, cli `coverage reads the map the way the renderer does`) run in Test UI and Test Core respectively, so the pins for M1 and S1 are measured by runs still open.

### ② Semver level

- Changesets unchanged from the first head: `@objectstack/spec` patch, `@object-ui/i18n` patch, both `Clause-②: no` / `Metadata-protocol: none`; PR body agrees; Check Changeset green on this head. Patch remains the right level; nothing in the delta widens, narrows or re-types a published surface.
- `Clause-②:` line: `no` — correct for the delta too (`check-changeset-no-major` grades by the PR-scoped declaration, and a bare `no` with every entry `patch` is consistent).
- **S1 — should-fix.** The delta changes `@objectstack/cli` behaviour (`check:i18n-coverage` now reports the Traditional entry for a Traditional reader of a two-script map) with no changeset naming `@objectstack/cli`. The gate does not demand one (it counts added changesets and judges declared level, not per-package coverage), and the `fixed` group bumps the cli patch regardless — but the release note for the coverage change is then missing from the cli's changelog, against the repo's own precedent of per-package `'@objectstack/cli': patch` notes (`29594-…`, `29873-…`, `29934-…`). Add `.changeset/30910-cli-i18n-coverage-script.md` with `'@objectstack/cli': patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. (`@object-ui/app-shell` is private; a note there is optional, precedent exists either way.)

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Live `zh-Hant` console check** — still NOT MEASURED by the dev; still owed to the seat before ACCEPT. The delta adds a second surface to it: in a `zh-Hant` Studio session, rename a nav item whose label is `{ en, zh, 'zh-TW' }` and confirm the field shows the new text and `zh` is untouched.
2. **Case asymmetry** (carrier: contract reviewer) — weighed on the first head, not escalated; the delta's cli change keeps it (`key.split('-')[0] === base` case-sensitive, then the resolver, also case-sensitive), as the cli docstring now states.
3. **Claim amendment 6700234158** names exactly the delta's four new paths; nothing outside it moved. Right.
4. **Prior findings, disposition:** M1 resolved (④); S1 resolved (④) with one caveat (④ S2); S2 (prose) resolved; S3 (one-script-map cross-script write) was "file, do not block" and is unchanged — the M1 fix deliberately preserves it (`{ zh }` at `zh-Hant` still writes `zh`, pinned as a control), so the card to file stands.
5. `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none` on the dev report — nothing in the delta changes that: `ownEntryKey` and `inlineLocaleText` both read own string properties only and hand the resolver maps they built themselves.

### ④ Design judgment
